extraction.name: EgoLife
extraction.description: A comprehensive ultra-long egocentric daily life dataset with multimodal egocentric video, synchronized third-person views, and intensive annotations, collected from six participants living together for one week to support egocentric AI assistants and long-context question answering.
extraction.creator: The EgoLife Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected over seven days in a custom-designed shared house where six volunteers lived together, wore Meta Aria glasses to capture multimodal egocentric video, and were additionally recorded by 15 GoPro cameras and millimeter-wave radars; activities included meetings, shopping, cooking, rehearsals, socializing, sightseeing, and party preparation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Direct measurement, Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes first-person video from AI glasses, third-person video from fixed indoor cameras, synchronized multimodal signal data including millimeter-wave radars and WiFi signals, plus IMU, gaze, audio, and VRS data.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After synchronization, audio from six participants was merged for speech recognition and diarization, then split back into six participant-specific tracks; initial narration phrases were merged with GPT-4o-mini into coherent captions and then expanded with representative frames and transcripts using GPT-4o into visual-audio captions; GPT-4o was also used to automatically categorize activities and generate QA candidates before human filtering and refinement.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data were synchronized across sources, cleaned for privacy and release readiness, desensitized by blurring faces, license plates, and sensitive screen content, muting sensitive audio, extracting and aligning multimodal signals with video, and processing audio for clarity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcript annotations were created by applying speech recognition and diarization to synchronized audio, then reviewed and refined by human reviewers per participant. Caption annotations were produced by splitting videos into 5-minute clips, slowing them to 0.8× speed, having annotators narrate continuously, transcribing and correcting the narration, then merging and expanding captions with GPT tools and human verification. QA annotations were generated by prompting GPT-4o on visual-audio captions to create candidate questions, then human annotators filtered, revised, selected final questions, generated distractors, and annotated audio requirement and look-back time.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: AI-generated QA candidates were not used directly; annotators filtered and refined them, retaining only questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior and preferring longer dependencies and real-world relevance. Final QA curation reduced about 100K candidates per participant to 1K for revision and then 500 final QAs per participant. Annotators also marked whether audio was needed and the certification/look-back length.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Speech recognition [Whisper Large v3/OpenAI Whisper], open-source diarization algorithm, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini for re-querying, CFAR detection algorithm for mmWave post-processing
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The project is ongoing, with future versions planned and continued annotation partnership; the authors plan to expand the dataset to more languages, locations, and activities, and the Milan subset will be detailed in an upcoming blog series.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Faces/identities, voices/speech, private or identifiable audio content, mobile/computer screen content, passwords or personal data on screens, vehicle license plates, language, location, and interpersonal interactions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and system could improve personalized assistance, contextual reminders, education, professional support, and aid for elderly or cognitively challenged individuals, but require privacy safeguards, transparency, and ethical consideration to maintain autonomy and trust.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The current dataset intentionally starts with a narrow setting, sacrificing some generalizability due to a single language/scenario focus; the personalized model can overfit to early observations such as clothing cues, causing identity misrecognition.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently has limited generalizability due to narrow setting and language coverage; recordings are segmented every three hours because of storage limits; current models still struggle with speech understanding, laughter/emotion understanding, identity recognition, and retrieval reasoning; the task remains challenging with substantial room for improvement.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for developing and benchmarking multimodal egocentric AI assistants, long-context life-oriented question answering, long-duration activity understanding, interpersonal dynamics analysis, contextual interaction modeling, training EgoGPT, automatically generating QA candidates, and evaluating systems on EgoLifeQA.

description.evidence: This effort resulted in the EgoLife Dataset, a comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation.

inLanguage.evidence: The primary language of the EgoLife dataset is Chinese1. All the annotations (transcripts, captions, QAs) are primarily in Chinese and translated into English.

isLiveDataset.evidence: This ongoing project aims to document human daily activities in natural environments

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The EgoLife dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment, called the EgoHouse (shown in Figure 1). Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses [1] and captured multimodal egocentric videos. To enhance the dataset with third-person perspectives, 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded the participants’ activities from multiple angles. Additionally, millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data, supporting synchronized, comprehensive multimodal analysis of daily events and interactions.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We conducted a comprehensive data collection study where six participants lived together for one week, continuously recording their daily activities... using AI glasses for multimodal egocentric video capture, along with synchronized third-person-view video references.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Each data instance includes: • First-person video from AI glasses • Third-person video from fixed indoor cameras • Synchronized multimodal signal data, including millimeter-wave radars and WiFi signals

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The EgoLife dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We started transcript annotation after synchronizing all the egocentric videos, merging audio tracks from six participants into one, and applying speech recognition [90] to generate initial timestamped transcripts... Afterward, we split the audio into six tracks, one for each participant... Using GPT-4o-mini, we merged related phrases into 25K “merged captions,” forming coherent sentences aligned with specific video segments. These captions were then expanded by pairing them with representative frames (sampled at 1 FPS) and corresponding transcripts, summarized by GPT-4o.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: A rigorous data cleaning process was implemented to ensure synchronization, participant privacy, and readiness for annotation and data release, as illustrated in Figure 4... De-identification Process All faces and sensitive visual data were blurred. Any sensitive topics in audio were muted to protect participant privacy.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We started transcript annotation after synchronizing all the egocentric videos... applying speech recognition [90] to generate initial timestamped transcripts... This 50-hour transcript was then reviewed for accuracy... Reviewers refined each track... The captioning tool is a video editing software with dubbing functions [92]. We split all the videos into 5-minute clips, which were slowed to 0.8 × speed, allowing annotators to provide continuous, detailed narrations... The narration was converted to text via a transcription tool, then reviewed and corrected... We crafted prompts for each type and fed “visual-audio captions” into GPT-4o in batches, generating around 100K timestamped questions per participant... these questions acted as a filtering and inspiration tool for annotators... Annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: The captioning tool is a video editing software with dubbing functions [92]... [92] ByteDance. Capcut, 2024. Mobile application software... These AI-generated questions were provided to annotators as SRT files, allowing them to view each question in sync with the relevant video segment.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Rather than serving as final annotations, these questions acted as a filtering and inspiration tool for annotators, helping them identify valuable instances. Only questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior were retained, with a preference for those demanding longer dependencies and strong real-world relevance... After a rigorous selection and refinement process, we filtered the 100K QA candidates down to 1K high-quality questions per participant... This final round of curation resulted in a carefully crafted set of 500 QA per participant. Annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions... Additionally, they annotated whether audio was required to answer the question and specified the look-back time (certification length)

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: applying speech recognition [90] to generate initial timestamped transcripts. Using an open-source diarization algorithm [91]... Using GPT-4o-mini, we merged related phrases into 25K “merged captions”... summarized by GPT-4o... We crafted prompts for each type and fed “visual-audio captions” into GPT-4o in batches... In the post-process of mmWave data, we used the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection algorithm

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Looking ahead, we plan to expand the dataset to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities... This ongoing project aims to document human daily activities in natural environments... this partnership will continue for future EgoLife versions... the Milan dataset has been collected and will be detailed in the upcoming EgoLife blog series.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: Blurring of faces and identifiers: All participant faces were blurred to anonymize identities. Additionally, bystanders’ faces and vehicle license plates appearing in the footage were thoroughly blurred. –Audio muting: Sensitive audio segments containing private or potentially identifiable information were muted... –Screen privacy: Frames containing sensitive screen content, such as mobile or computer screens, were reviewed, and any private information was blurred. For example, visible screens displaying passwords or personal data underwent detailed masking processes.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The development of EgoButler and the EgoLifeQA dataset holds significant potential to enhance human-AI interaction, particularly in personalized assistance and context-aware applications... improving quality of life, especially for individuals needing consistent support, such as the elderly or those with cognitive challenges... However, as this technology integrates more deeply into personal spaces, it is essential to address privacy and ethical considerations to ensure user autonomy and trust.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: As the first step toward a realistic egocentric life assistant, we intentionally started with a narrow setting to build a strong foundation, sacrificing some generalizability (e.g., single language/scenario)... Since it was fine-tuned on EgoLife Day-1, it tends to overfit to early observations. For example, if a person wore a blue shirt on Day-1, EgoGPT may misidentify a different person wearing blue later as the same individual

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Due to storage limitations, recordings are structured into three-hour segments... As the first step toward a realistic egocentric life assistant, we intentionally started with a narrow setting to build a strong foundation, sacrificing some generalizability (e.g., single language/scenario)... EgoGPT’s speech understanding remains incomplete. It struggles to understand human laughter and emotions... Identity recognition is another challenge... the task remains inherently challenging, and there is still a large room for improvement.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: These comprehensive annotations enable the development of state-of-the-art multimodal egocentric AI assistants and introduce novel tasks to advance long-term egocentric life assistance... These captions serve two main purposes: training EgoGPT and automatically generating QA candidates for the next section... Building on the EgoLife dataset, we introduce the EgoLifeQA benchmark
